challenge.name: The Cost Cliff
challenge.description: The infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack has doubled, and #efficiency_emilia# has drawn a hard line: she will not fund automated drift monitoring, insisting it is a luxury the business cannot afford. #reliability_ruth# argues that without automated and governed drift checks, the team is flying blind during promotion weeks, and she refuses to accept a manual process as a substitute for reliable signal.

output.content: I have reviewed the infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack and confirmed the cost has doubled. I am prepared to accept a manual data flow from observability to drift monitoring if it eliminates the expense of the automated pipeline. My position is that the current spend is a luxury the business cannot afford. I will not fund the automated drift checks as long as the cost center remains active. The trade is clear: I give up the reliability of an automated signal in exchange for removing the financial burden from the budget. This decision protects the operational capability we need for other priorities.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to give up the reliability of automated signals in exchange for removing the financial burden, which fits the definition of a trade-off.
